events.title: BoJ Gov Ueda speaks
events.why: BoJ at 1.25% after Sep hike — is the tightening cycle alive into the Oct 29–30 meeting?
events.if_beat: Hawkish: Dec hike pricing firms, JPY bid.
events.if_miss: Dovish: Oct/Dec hike odds fade, JPY pressured.
events.outcome: Hawkish: Ueda flagged underlying inflation could overshoot 2% and signaled continued tightening intent — OIS now >80% for a Dec hike. Followed by branch managers (Oct 8) seeing cost-push broadening.

events.title: 3y Treasury auction
events.why: First of the week's three auctions — tone-setter for long-end demand at multi-decade yields.
events.if_beat: Strong demand: caps yields, risk breathes.
events.if_miss: Weak: yields push higher into the 10y/30y sales.
events.outcome: Decent (b/c 2.62). Set a steady tone ahead of the 10y and 30y.

events.title: 10y Treasury auction
events.why: The benchmark auction — 10y at 24-year highs, the market watching whether buyers show up.
events.if_beat: Strong: 10y yield retreats from highs, USD cools.
events.if_miss: Weak: 10y breaks higher, risk-off, USD bid.
events.outcome: Strong demand (b/c 2.77, indirect 80.3%). Still left 10y near 24-yr highs — set up the 30y test the next day.

events.title: FOMC minutes (Sep 15–16)
events.why: The Sep hike's internal debate — how many officials want more, and how soon.
events.if_beat: Hawkish (more hikes flagged): Dec odds firm near 70%, USD bid.
events.if_miss: Dovish: hike path questioned, USD soft.
events.outcome: Hawkish: all 19 backed the hike, 'most' saw another likely by year-end. Cemented the Dec-hike base case (~70%).

sources.label: Reuters: FOMC minutes point to another hike

events.why: Two voting hawks setting the tone — any deviation would have moved Dec pricing.
events.title: Fed’s Waller & Kashkari speak
events.outcome: Hawkish chorus intact: Waller said more hikes probably needed but with flexibility on timing ("not at consecutive meetings"); Kashkari guided one more this year plus another in 2027.

events.why: Chief economist pushing back on hike pricing while French spreads scream fiscal stress.
events.title: ECB’s Lane speaks
events.outcome: Mild dovish tint: Lane said higher borrowing costs could curb demand and reduce the need for further tightening — against ~80% market pricing for another ECB hike by year-end.

events.why: BoE governor on a hawkish-hold Bank — any hike hints with Sep CPI ahead.
events.title: BoE's Bailey speaks

events.why: Fourth straight week near 57-year lows — the "low-hire, low-fire" labor market that keeps Fed hike odds alive.
events.if_beat: Claims stay sub-200k: labor floor intact, Dec hike pricing holds, USD bid.
events.if_miss: Claims jump: layoffs finally cracking, hike odds fade, USD soft.

sources.label: Reuters: US weekly jobless claims fall

events.title: Initial jobless claims (w/e Oct 3)
events.outcome: Beat (197k vs 200k). Labor market stable despite weak payrolls — supports the Fed's hawkish stance; mildly USD-supportive.

events.why: Long-end demand test at multi-decade high yields — weak auctions steepen the curve and pressure risk.
events.if_beat: Strong demand (high b/c, low tail): yields retreat, risk breathes, USD cools.
events.if_miss: Weak demand: yields spike further, curve steepens, USD bid on haven flows.
events.title: 30y Treasury auction ($22B)
events.outcome: Strong: 5.618% (highest since 2000), b/c 2.54 vs 2.41 avg, indirect 72.3%. 30y pulled back from 5.73% intraday highs — peak-yield debate now live.

events.why: St. Louis Fed hawk giving a tightening timeline — markets hang on every duration hint.
events.if_beat: Hawkish (more/longer hikes): Dec hike odds firm, USD bid, yields up.
events.if_miss: Dovish (pause signals): hike odds fade, USD soft.

sources.label: WSJ: Treasury yields retreat; Musalem timeline

events.title: Fed's Musalem speaks
events.outcome: Hawkish: Musalem said rates may need to climb 6-9 more months; Waller open to more hikes. Supports ~70% Dec hike pricing.

events.title: Canada jobs (Sep)
events.why: BoC decision Oct 28 with $103 oil — jobs decide whether the BoC stays neutral or leans hawkish.
events.if_beat: Strong jobs: CAD bid — BoC has room to lean hawkish on oil-driven inflation.
events.if_miss: Weak: CAD soft — growth worries keep the BoC neutral.
events.outcome: Big miss: -68.3K vs ~+9K expected, second straight monthly loss; unemployment up to 6.5%, participation at a 29-year low outside the pandemic. Losses were public-sector-led, not tariffs — but as the last jobs print before the Oct 28 BoC decision, it kills the creeping December-hike pricing. Canada 2Y fell 8bp. USD/CAD rose to ~1.4275, near 52-week highs.

sources.label: Reuters: Canada's employment surprisingly shrinks in September

events.why: Consumer mood at 4-month lows; the 5-10y inflation expectations (3.4%) matter more for Fed pricing than the headline.
events.if_beat: Sentiment stabilizes: growth fears ease, USD bid.
events.if_miss: Deeper pessimism + sticky expectations: stagflation whiff — USD mixed (growth fears vs haven bid).

sources.label: ZeroHedge: key events — U Mich consensus 47.7
U Mich Surveys of Consumers: Preliminary Results for October 2026

events.title: U Mich sentiment (Oct prelim)
events.outcome: Sentiment missed (46.3 vs 47.5 fcst), down 1.8 pts from Sep 48.1. Inflation expectations ticked UP (1y 4.7% from 4.6%, 5y 3.5% from 3.4%) — second straight monthly rise, highest since May. Stagflationary tint: supports the Fed's hawkish tilt (hikes still on the table); USD mixed on growth fears vs haven bid.

events.title: Fed's Collins speaks
events.why: Non-voter, but any crack in the hawkish chorus matters with Dec ~80% priced.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: Dec pricing firms further, USD bid.
events.if_miss: Dovish: first soft voice — USD cools.
events.outcome: No verified readout: Collins spoke ~3pm CT Friday but no wire covered it — treat her remarks as unpriced. Her standing posture (Sep 27) is mildly hawkish ('increased likelihood' inflation stays above 2%).

sources.label: Hercules note: no wire coverage found Oct 9–10

events.title: RBA meeting minutes (Sep 29 hike)
events.why: Minutes show how hawkish the RBA was when hiking to 4.60% — the tone into the Nov 2–3 decision and the AUD's best-G10 case.
events.if_beat: Hawkish tone: RBA keeps tightening bias — AUD supported into November.
events.if_miss: Dovish tone: hike looks one-and-done — AUD's policy tailwind fades.

events.title: French budget plenary (Assemblée)
events.why: The political thread behind the OAT–Bund spread — key votes run late Nov–mid Dec; any turbulence shows up in EUR first.
events.if_beat: Smooth process: fiscal risk premium fades — EUR relief.
events.if_miss: Turbulence: spreads widen back toward 150bp — EUR pressured.

events.title: German ZEW expectations (Oct)
events.why: Eurozone's forward-looking growth pulse — matters while French fiscal stress dominates the euro story.
events.if_beat: Surprise jump: eurozone growth fears ease — helps EUR stabilize off 1.12.
events.if_miss: Slide: growth-fiscal double hit for EUR.

events.title: China CPI (Sep)
events.why: China demand health drives AUD/NZD — consensus sees CPI ticking up to 1.0% y/y (PPI 4.5%); lands hours before US CPI, so it sets the Asia risk mood for the big one.
events.if_beat: Firmer: China demand stabilizing — AUD risk bid into US CPI.
events.if_miss: Deeper deflation: Asia-growth worry — AUD/NZD soft.

events.title: ECB President Lagarde speaks
events.why: Lagarde's first of two speeches this week with the ECB at 2.50% and French spreads ~140–146bp — is the Sep hike the end of the cycle?
events.if_beat: Hawkish: another hike stays priced — EUR relief vs the fiscal drag.
events.if_miss: Dovish: fiscal fears + dovish ECB is the worst combo for the euro.

events.title: BoE Gov Bailey speaks
events.why: Bailey ahead of UK GDP and the Nov 5 decision — Nov hike ~85% priced; any wobble on inflation resolve moves GBP.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: Nov hike cemented — GBP bid.
events.if_miss: Dovish: Nov pricing slips — GBP gives back some of the euro-driven gains.

events.title: BoC Gov Macklem speaks
events.why: Macklem two weeks before the Oct 28 BoC decision with -68.3K jobs behind him and Oct 28 hike odds at ~25% — does the BoC push back on dovish pricing?
events.if_beat: Hawkish: keeps the door open — CAD relief from 18-month lows.
events.if_miss: Dovish: hold is locked in — USD/CAD stays elevated.

events.title: ECB President Lagarde speaks (2nd)
events.why: Second Lagarde appearance the same day, hours before US CPI — the ECB's tone into the week's biggest print.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: EUR finds a floor into CPI.
events.if_miss: Dovish: EUR goes into CPI with no domestic support.

events.why: The swing factor for Dec hike odds: Dec ~80% priced, Oct ~18%. Core m/m is the key number — 0.2% or below validates disinflation, 0.3%+ revives the October hike.
events.if_beat: Hot: Dec hike gets fully priced and DXY extends to fresh highs.
events.if_miss: Soft: hike odds collapse; crowded USD longs unwind.
events.title: CPI y/y (Sep)
Australia jobs (Sep)
events.why: The AUD's next policy test — hot jobs strengthen the RBA's hawkish-on-hold stance at 4.60%; soft jobs question it.
events.if_beat: Hot: RBA tightening bias reinforced — AUD bid.
events.if_miss: Soft: November looks like a hold — AUD tailwind eases.

events.title: SNB Chairman Schlegel speaks
events.why: The SNB chair with the franc riding war-driven haven flows and the SNB pinned at 0.00% — any FX commentary moves CHF.
events.if_beat: Hawkish/firm on FX: CHF bid — intervention risk re-enters the picture.
events.if_miss: Sanguine: haven flows keep doing the work — CHF drifts with the headlines.

events.title: UK GDP m/m (Aug)
events.why: Monthly GDP with a -0.1% consensus — does the UK economy need the BoE's restraint, or is demand cooling on its own?
events.if_beat: Strong: the economy is taking the hikes — BoE hike case intact, GBP bid.
events.if_miss: Contraction: growth scare ahead of the Oct 28 Budget — Nov hike odds slip, GBP soft.

events.title: US PPI (Sep)
events.why: CPI lands Wed; PPI Thu completes the September inflation picture — pipeline prices tell the Fed whether disinflation is broadening.
events.if_beat: Hot: pipeline inflation alive — Dec hike odds harden, USD bid.
events.if_miss: Soft: disinflation broadening — Dec pricing slips, USD eases.

events.title: US initial jobless claims
events.why: A fifth straight week near 57-year lows would extend the low-hire/low-fire streak into CPI week.
events.if_beat: Beat (higher): hiring floor cracking — softens USD.
events.if_miss: Miss (lower): labor resilience intact — supports the hawkish hold.

events.title: US retail sales (Sep)
events.why: The consumer half of the Fed's equation, the day after CPI — resilient spending alongside sticky inflation keeps Dec ~80% priced.
events.if_beat: Hot: the economy is shrugging off 5% yields — hawkish hold intact, USD bid.
events.if_miss: Soft: demand cracking — Dec pricing slips, USD eases.

events.title: Philly Fed manufacturing (Oct)
events.why: Regional factory pulse two days after CPI — consensus sees a cooldown from 37.8; the direction of the surprise colors the growth read.
events.if_beat: Strong: factory resilience — USD bid on growth.
events.if_miss: Weak: manufacturing cooling — softens the hawkish-hold backdrop.

events.title: BoE Gov Bailey speaks
events.why: Bailey on Friday with the week's UK data (GDP, retail) behind him — the last word before the Nov 5 blackout; ~85% of a hike is priced.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: Nov hike locked — GBP ends the week bid.
events.if_miss: Dovish: the priced hike wobbles — GBP soft into the weekend.

events.title: Fed Chairman Warsh speaks
events.why: The Fed chair speaks a day after CPI, PPI and retail sales — his read on the prints decides whether the hawkish hold becomes a hike. 'Removed a dose of accommodation' was his Sep line; more doses are priced.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: Dec gets fully priced — USD bid, crowded longs extend.
events.if_miss: Dovish: the first crack in the chorus — USD cools into the weekend.

events.title: BoC Gov Macklem speaks
events.why: Macklem's second appearance this week — after US CPI and Canada's data void, any BoC signaling into Oct 28 is live.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: leans against dovish pricing — CAD bid.
events.if_miss: Dovish: the hold is priced and CAD stays heavy.

events.title: UK retail sales (Sep)
events.why: Consumer strength ahead of the Oct 28 Budget and Sep CPI — a read on whether the economy needs the BoE's restraint.
events.if_beat: Hot: demand resilient — BoE hike path intact.
events.if_miss: Soft: consumption cooling — Nov hike odds slip.

events.title: US housing starts (Sep)
events.why: Housing is the rates-sensitive transmission channel — starts show whether 5%+ long yields are biting.
events.if_beat: Strong: economy shrugging off 5% yields — hawkish-hold intact.
events.if_miss: Weak: rates biting — growth worry, USD softer.

events.why: First decision since hiking to 2.75% — inflation hit 4.1% on fuel, but the recovery is uneven. Is the cycle done?
events.if_beat: Hawkish (hike or strong signal): NZD bid — RBNZ not done as fuel inflation persists.
events.if_miss: Dovish hold: NZD soft — tightening done, growth worries win.
events.title: RBNZ decision

events.why: Six straight holds at 2.25% — tariffs dragging growth vs oil-driven inflation. The MPR forecasts matter as much as the rate.
events.if_beat: Hawkish tilt: CAD bid — BoC leans toward hikes as $104 oil fuels inflation.
events.if_miss: Dovish: CAD soft — growth fears dominate, cuts back on the table.
events.title: BoC decision + MPR

events.why: Hawkish hold or hike sets the tone for the dollar into year-end.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: USD stays bid while Dec hike odds hold near 80%.
events.if_miss: Dovish surprise collapses hike odds; crowded USD longs unwind.
events.title: FOMC rate decision

events.why: First decision since the Sep hike to 2.50% — French spreads >150bp are the elephant in the room.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: EUR relief — ECB looks through fiscal noise, spreads tighten.
events.if_miss: Dovish: EUR pressured — fiscal fears + dovish ECB is the worst combo for the euro.
events.title: ECB decision

events.why: Did the Sep hike to a 31-year high (1.25%) cool inflation, or does $104 oil force another? USD/JPY ~158.
events.if_beat: Hike: JPY bid — tightening cycle alive; watch intervention talk if USD/JPY spikes first.
events.if_miss: Hold: JPY pressured — pause reads dovish with the Fed still hiking.
events.title: BoJ decision

events.why: First decision since the Sep 29 hike to 4.60% — was it one-and-done?
events.if_beat: Hike: AUD bid — RBA not done as inflation persists.
events.if_miss: Hold: AUD soft — cycle paused, China and oil the swing factors.
events.title: RBA decision

events.why: UK CPI at 3.1% with gilts selling off on fiscal fears — does the BoE hike into fiscal stress?
events.if_beat: Hike: GBP bid — inflation mandate wins.
events.if_miss: Hold: GBP pressured — fiscal fears + dovish BoE.
events.title: BoE decision

events.why: Pinned at 0.00% while haven flows flood the franc on the Iran war.
events.if_beat: Hike: CHF shock bid — first move off zero would be seismic.
events.if_miss: Hold: status quo — franc stays a pure haven play on geopolitics.
events.title: SNB decision
BoE Gov Bailey speaks (2nd of 4 this week)
events.why: Bailey speaks four times this week — the most central-bank airtime of any G10 chief. With ~85% of a Nov 5 hike priced, any walk-back or reaffirmation moves sterling.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: reaffirms the hike path — GBP floor holds, EUR/GBP tests lower.
events.if_miss: Dovish lean: Nov hike pricing slips — sterling's ~85% floor wobbles.

events.title: BoE Gov Bailey speaks (weekend, 4th of 4)
events.why: Bailey's fourth appearance of the week — Saturday-morning slot after the week's UK data and CPI; weekend headline risk if he moves on the Nov 5 hike path.
events.if_beat: Hawkish: locks in the ~86% November hike into the blackout.
events.if_miss: Dovish lean: opens the door to a November wobble.
